trigger: FAQ Q4 confirms prompt IDs 1,2,3 have hidden correction values that must be learned from public feedback.

policy.base: P9 public-greedy candidate boundary with its existing conservative structure rule; P8 fixed-prompt rollout and P10 complete plans are excluded after prompt selection.
policy.probe_nodes: Select at most two public peace/neutral, unused, in-bound, lowest-degree nodes using select_prompt_probe_nodes.
policy.early_stop: After one complete uncensored node, stop when PromptCalibrationLedger has a provisional best set or all three normalized values are equal and nonzero; the latter gives tied-prompt magnitude without strict ordering. Use a second node only after all-zero, clipping, incomplete evidence, or probe failure. Preserve provisional/confident distinction.
policy.prediction: Average one public normalized first-slot response for the selected prompt from every complete uncensored probe node, including an all-zero node; use later selected-prompt first-equivalent responses once per node to update that population prior. Never divide by a presumed prompt strength and never use P8's hard-coded 15 scenarios.
policy.actions: Every probe and later action is a Python-generated legal candidate selected by the injected LLM; at most one environment action per host step.
policy.fallback: Probe failure, clipping without usable evidence, conflict, or estimator error falls back to original P9. Prompt histories from IDs 2/3 are never pooled into a prompt-1 first-response estimate.
policy.all_negative: If the empirically best prompt prior is nonpositive, generate no communication candidate; select a positive exact structural action or stop.

comparison: End-to-end candidate including real probe cost versus the unchanged P9 ZIP with no probes.
required_prompt_cases: all prompts tied at the same positive or negative nonzero correction
all prompts and/or the first node response tied at zero
zero-response first probe node followed by informative second node
